supremeCourt.name: Suprema Corte de Justicia
supremeCourt.appointmentMethod: Elected by a two-thirds majority of the General Assembly; 10-year terms.
supremeCourt.fspEraChanges: No court-packing. The court remained independent during FA governments — notably its 2013 ruling striking down parts of a law on prosecution of past (dictatorship-era) crimes ran against the FA government’s position.
supremeCourt.stillServing: Membership rotates on fixed 10-year terms; no FSP-driven structural change — a contrast case of judicial independence.

courtHistory.event: The modern SCJ dates to 1907; the 1973–1985 civic-military dictatorship subordinated the judiciary, restored at the 1985 transition.
Under the traditional (Colorado/Nacional) governments the 5-member SCJ operated normally; members elected by a 2/3 majority of the General Assembly.

Across the FA governments (2005–2020, 2025–) there was NO court-packing; the court kept its independence — notably its 2013 ruling striking down parts of a law on prosecuting dictatorship-era crimes ran AGAINST the FA government's position.

supremeCourt.justicesNote: Five justices on fixed 10-year terms, elected by a 2/3 Assembly majority; individual members rotate and are not itemized here.
